item.description:
You can paste into the capture panel

⌘V now works — and so do ⌘X, ⌘C, ⌘Z and ⌘A. They never did before, which is worth explaining: on macOS these are menu commands rather than something text fields do on their own, and Crisper had no menu for them to live in. Copying a link to save it and finding you had to retype it was the single roughest edge in 0.1.0.

Keyboard shortcuts

  • ⌘N — new capture, whenever Crisper has focus.
  • ⌘F — jump straight to search in the main window.
  • ⌘W and ⌘M — close and minimise the window.
  • ⌘Q — quit, without hunting through the "•••" menu.

⌃Space still opens the capture panel from any app, and still does not interrupt what you are doing.

Updates

Check for Updates… now sits in the Crisper menu, beside About. Crisper checks quietly on its own once a day, downloads in the background, and then waits — you will find an Install Update line in the menu when one is ready, never a window in front of your work. You always see what changed before anything is installed.

One thing you will notice

While the main window is open, Crisper appears in the Dock and in the menu bar at the top of the screen — that is simply how macOS gives an app menus at all. Close the window and it goes back to being only the icon in your menu bar. The capture panel never does this: ⌃Space still opens it without taking you out of what you are doing.

Smaller things

  • The installer window now shows you where to drag the app, instead of two bare icons.
  • Crisper identifies itself to macOS as a productivity app, so it files correctly in Launchpad and Spotlight.
